precepts.text: If a soul hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity. Whatever the judgment is on that man, you get the judgment. This is why in the hood people see murders and say I'm not saying nothing, and later end up dead themselves; they were a witness that chose not to utter it. Story told in class: at camp a brother was told to trim his hair and answered, I guess I'm not traveling then; men heard it, and the officer who heard it first said, I was going to tell you next week. Fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me. Be mindful of brothers; you got to be mindful of the things they say or don't say.
precepts.point: But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon's faction murders were committed: Simon hated Onias so much he had one of his men kill one of Onias's priests. That is why I say it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
“And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.”

What does that mean? Whatever the judgment is on that man, you get the judgment. This is why in the hood, in the ghetto, people see murders all the time and say, I’m not saying nothing. Then weeks later, a month, a year, that same person ends up dead, and you say, what did she do, they never killed nobody. No: they were a witness, and they chose not to utter it.

Read on and the law also says “if a soul swear, pronouncing with his lips to do evil, or to do good, whatsoever it be that a man shall pronounce with an oath, and it be hid from him; when he knoweth of it, then he shall be guilty in one of these.” And when he is guilty, “he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing”.

A story from camp: the brothers were planning who to take traveling, and one brother’s hair was unkempt. He was told to trim it, and he answered, well, I guess I’m not traveling then. A couple of men heard it. A young man from Detroit told what was said, and when the officer who heard it first was questioned the next week, he said, I heard it, I was going to tell you next week. Fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me.

Be mindful of brothers. They may seem decent on the outside, but you have to be mindful of the things they say, or don’t say.

precepts.text: A witness that does not utter what he has seen bears his own iniquity; Joseph uttered the evil report according to that law.
precepts.point: Joseph brought unto his father the evil report of his brethren. That was law, not tale bearing: if a soul hear swearing and be a witness and do not utter it, he shall bear his iniquity. The law was already around, and Joseph kept it.

note.label: Genesis 37: Joseph the Dreamer

precepts.why:
“And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.” A witness that does not utter what he has seen bears his own iniquity.

So when Joseph “brought unto his father their evil report”, that was law, not tale bearing. The law was already around, and Joseph kept it by uttering what he had seen.

precepts.text: I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel; hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.
precepts.point: There is a way to correct: brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness. A soft answer turneth away wrath; you do not render evil for evil and blast a brother, you build him up with a humble mind, and that is how souls are won. The man gathering sticks got the reproof that fit that willful case; meekness fits the brother overtaken in a fault.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
“Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.”

The watchman does not cover his eyes, because he needs to see, and does not cover his mouth, because he gives the warning. That is the witness of Leviticus 5:1: he has seen or known of it, and he must utter it. Hear no evil, see no evil, speak no evil is a wicked saying; the scriptures say you renounce evil. If you know and say nothing, your brother’s blood is required because you did nothing about it.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.”

If you do not apply Leviticus 5:1 and utter what you witnessed, you hate your brother in your heart. Keeping quiet at his sin, or trimming your ways for him, is hate too. We are to rebuke one another and not suffer sin upon a brother.

Stand still for the laws of the Most High and do not turn your ways for anybody, even carnal family that puts you out over your beard or your fringes.

precepts.text: Enquire diligently, and behold, if it be true and the thing certain; the diligent enquiry that governs how the witness law is applied.
precepts.point: A lot of people do not know how to apply this verse; the precept for Leviticus 5:1 is Deuteronomy 17:4. Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed: make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
A lot of people do not know how to apply Leviticus 5:1, and this is its precept. “And it be told thee, and thou hast heard of it, and enquired diligently, and, behold, it be true, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought in Israel”.

Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed. The witness who has seen or known of it must utter it, but make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment.

precepts.text: What have I to do to judge them also that are without? them that are without God judgeth; the law is applied among the body, not the world.
precepts.point: A lot of people do not know how to apply this verse; the precept for Leviticus 5:1 is Deuteronomy 17:4. Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed: make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
The witness law was written when Israel was in its own kingdom and everyone lived by the law. Today it is applied among those in the body that understand the law, not to the world outside. Paul draws the line: not to keep company “if any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner; with such an one no not to eat.”

“For what have I to do to judge them also that are without? do not ye judge them that are within? But them that are without God judgeth. Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person.” The Most High judges them that are without, so the neighbor selling drugs on the corner is not your business; but when you see sin among Israel, do not hide it, bring it out, send it up to the leadership or correct it yourself.

precepts.text: A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him; do not hide sin among Israel, bring it out.
precepts.point: A lot of people do not know how to apply this verse; the precept for Leviticus 5:1 is Deuteronomy 17:4. Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed: make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
“A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.”

Let no man stay him: do not hide sin among Israel, bring it out. The witness who has seen or known of it and does not utter it is staying the guilty man, and he shall bear his iniquity.

precepts.text: Make a chain, for the land is full of bloody crimes; that is what came upon Jerusalem when this law was not applied among the people.
precepts.point: A lot of people do not know how to apply this verse; the precept for Leviticus 5:1 is Deuteronomy 17:4. Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed: make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
This is what came upon Jerusalem when the witness law was not applied among the people. The Lord gave the city “into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a spoil”, turned His face from them, and the robbers entered His secret place and defiled it.

“Make a chain: for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.” A land full of bloody crimes is a land where those who saw and knew did not utter it. When sin among Israel is hidden instead of brought out, the whole city fills with violence and the Most High hands it over.

precepts.text: Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not, when they defile my tabernacle; the defilement laws guarded the sacrifice.
precepts.point: The touching itself pertained to the sacrifice: Israel was separated from their uncleanness that they die not when they defile the tabernacle, so a man that had touched the unclean thing could not come in to sacrifice. There is no more sacrifice, so the touching-defilement laws do not apply today; a brush of boar bristles is not sin.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
The touching itself pertained to the sacrifice. “Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness; that they die not in their uncleanness, when they defile my tabernacle that is among them.” A man that had touched the unclean thing could not come in to sacrifice; the defilement laws guarded the tabernacle, that Israel die not.

Touching the carcase of an unclean beast or the uncleanness of man goes into eating, not mere contact. It is the same as telling your son or daughter, get your hand out of the cookie jar: you say do not touch it, not do not eat it, because you know what the intention is. The Lord deals with us the same way; do not be touching that stuff means do not eat it, do not defile yourself.

There is no more sacrifice, so the touching-defilement laws do not apply today; a brush of boar bristles is not sin.

precepts.text: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin.
precepts.point: A man was held accountable for whatever came out of his mouth; pronouncing with his lips and not performing it was sin. When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it, for better is it that thou shouldest not vow than that thou shouldest vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin. Christ set the same standard on the mouth: let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
A man was held accountable for whatever came out of his mouth; pronouncing with his lips and not performing it was sin. “When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.”

“Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?” Brothers say, I swear to God; watch your mouth. The soul that swore and did not perform had to confess that he had sinned in that thing and bring his trespass offering.

precepts.text: Let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.
precepts.point: A man was held accountable for whatever came out of his mouth; pronouncing with his lips and not performing it was sin. When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it, for better is it that thou shouldest not vow than that thou shouldest vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin. Christ set the same standard on the mouth: let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
Christ set the same standard on the mouth: “let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.”

Pronouncing with the lips to do evil or to do good with an oath is the more than these. Better not to swear at all than to be guilty in one of these and need a lamb or a kid of the goats for atonement.

precepts.text: Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices; I commanded not burnt offerings, but this thing: obey my voice, and I will be your God.
precepts.point: Israel took the nourishment of the Lord for granted, and he grew tired of the empty offerings: put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. He spake not unto our fathers concerning burnt offerings, but this thing commanded he: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people. He never wanted the sacrifices above obedience; today he does not want an apology or money in the plate, he wants you to obey his voice and repent.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
The offerings were the collateral of those times, scaled to what a man could bring, and families felt the after-effects of always sacrificing: the livestock and the agriculture went for your sins, and the household lacked because of it. Israel took the nourishment of the Lord for granted, and He grew tired of the empty offerings.

“Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.”

He never wanted the sacrifices above obedience. Today He does not want an apology or money in the plate; He wants you to obey His voice and repent.

precepts.text: Doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? He that keepeth thy soul knoweth whether the ignorance is real.
precepts.point: The scripture that pops up again is the same one: if thou sayest, behold, we knew it not, doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? Worldly family and coworkers that are not keeping the laws talk the same way, not understanding they condemn themselves because they are not repenting; that card cannot be pulled on the Messiah.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
Sin through ignorance in the holy things of the Lord, and the scripture that pops up again is the same one: “If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?”

He that keepeth thy soul knows whether the ignorance is real. Worldly family and coworkers that are not keeping the laws talk the same way, we knew it not, not understanding they condemn themselves because they are not repenting. That card cannot be pulled on the Messiah.

precepts.text: Meditate continually in his commandments, and he shall establish thine heart and give thee wisdom.
precepts.point: Stay humble with it: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty; neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me; David behaved and quieted himself as a child that is weaned of his mother. Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven; so behave yourselves humbly, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
Though he wist it not, yet is he guilty: saying I did not know does not remove sin. The remedy is to know the law. “Let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish thine heart, and give thee wisdom at thine owns desire.”

The ordinances are found in the first five books. As these four chapters a day are conducted, meditate and study them continually, and He will establish thine heart and give thee wisdom.

precepts.text: As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby; the milk is the first five books.

Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven; so behave yourselves humbly, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby”. The milk is the dos and the don’ts, the first five books.

Many want to run to Revelation and the parables, but the solutions for what is wrong in your spirit, for lust, covetousness, hatred, malice, and envy, sit in the ordinances and the commandments. Look up the scriptures on patience, temperance, and how to treat your family correctly. That is how a soul stops trespassing against the Lord through ignorance.

precepts.why:
Stay humble with it. “Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me. Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child.”

David behaved and quieted himself as a weaned child. Desiring the milk of the word instead of running to things too high for you is that same humble spirit.

Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven; so behave yourselves humbly, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom.

The disciples asked who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven, and Christ called a little child and set him in the midst of them: “Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.”

So behave yourselves humbly, as newborn babes desiring the milk of the word, as a child weaned of his mother, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom.

precepts.text: If a soul hear swearing and is a witness and do not utter it, he shall bear his iniquity; wickedness seen must be exposed.
precepts.point: Sin brings judgment on a whole house. Achan coveted the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver, and the wedge of gold, and he and his sons and his daughters and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

note.label: Leviticus 20: The Judgments Appointed for the Abominations

precepts.why:
“if the people of the land do any ways hide their eyes from the man, when he giveth of his seed unto Molech, and kill him not”, the Most High set His face against that man and against his family. Looking away is not an option.

“if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.” A witness that holds his peace bears iniquity. When you see wickedness you must utter it and expose it.

precepts.text: If a soul hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, and do not utter it, he shall bear his iniquity; utter what you know instead of concealing it.
precepts.point: This is why Leviticus 5:1 is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
“And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.” This is why Leviticus 5:1 is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Of the one who entices to other gods the law says “neither shalt thou conceal him”, meaning hide him; when wickedness is concealed, the whole nation is put in jeopardy. When it is uttered and dealt with, “all Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall do no more any such wickedness as this is among you.”

Many grew up on snitches get stitches. But in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. The witness who does not utter what he knows bears the iniquity himself; utter what you know instead of concealing it. It is that simple.

precepts.text: If a soul hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, and do not utter it, he shall bear his iniquity; the witness law is applied through the diligent enquiry of Deuteronomy 17:4.
precepts.point: Make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment; only after diligent enquiry was the man or woman brought to the gates and stoned with stones till they die.

note.label: Deuteronomy 17: Idolatry Judged and the Duty of a King

precepts.why:
“And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.” A lot of people do not know how to apply Leviticus 5:1; the precept for it is Deuteronomy 17:4.

The witness who has seen or known of a thing must utter it, and here is what is done with what he utters: “And it be told thee, and thou hast heard of it, and enquired diligently, and, behold, it be true, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought in Israel”. Whether it be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only if it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed.

So the witness law of Leviticus is applied through the diligent enquiry of Deuteronomy 17:4. Make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment; only after diligent enquiry was the man or woman that served other gods, the sun or moon or any of the host of heaven, brought to the gates and stoned with stones till they die.

precepts.text: If a soul hear the voice of swearing and is a witness, he must utter it; hence if we hear of violence we make it known.
precepts.point: Understand the frame: we live peaceably with all men and lay hands on no one; we do not incite or condone any violence, and if we hear of any we report it. The day of Psalms 137 has not yet come; it belongs to the return of the Lord, so chill out and relax, none of that is for now.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
“And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.” A soul that hears and is a witness must utter it, or he bears the iniquity himself.

Hence if we hear of any violence, we report it and make it known. We do not incite it and we do not condone it.

precepts.text: Sin is when a soul commits any of the things forbidden to be done by the Commandments of the Most High.
precepts.point: We are not going to stand before the Most High and be justified talking about "me and Jesus." If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God. Wearing pants, not wearing fringes, crossdressing; none of that will be excused.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
What is sin? “And if a soul sin, and commit any of these things which are forbidden to be done by the commandments of the Lord; though he wist it not, yet is he guilty, and shall bear his iniquity.” Sin is when a soul commits any of the things forbidden to be done by the Commandments of the Most High, and even if he did not know it, he is guilty and bears his iniquity.

So when David says “Against thee, thee only, have I sinned”, the sin is measured by the commandments. That is why wearing pants, not wearing fringes and crossdressing will not be excused: they are forbidden by the Commandments, and not knowing does not clear a man.

points: If a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it, if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity. Verse 4 defines the voice of swearing: a soul that swears, pronouncing with his lips to do evil or to do good. If you know and say nothing, your brother's blood is required because you did nothing about it.

We are to rebuke one another. Hear no evil, see no evil, speak no evil is a wicked saying; the scriptures say you renounce evil. The watchman does not cover his eyes, because he needs to see, and does not cover his mouth, because he gives the warning; hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.

If you do not apply this verse, you hate your brother in your heart; keeping quiet at his sin, or trimming your ways for him, is hate too. Stand still for the laws of the Most High and do not turn your ways for anybody, even carnal family that puts you out over your beard or your fringes.

There is a way to correct: brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness. A soft answer turneth away wrath; you do not render evil for evil and blast a brother, you build him up with a humble mind, and that is how souls are won. The man gathering sticks got the reproof that fit that willful case; meekness fits the brother overtaken in a fault.

The witness law was written when Israel was in its own kingdom and everyone lived by the law; today it is applied among those in the body that understand the law, not to the world outside. The Most High judges them that are without, so the neighbor selling drugs on the corner is not your business; but when you see sin among Israel, do not hide it, bring it out, send it up to the leadership or correct it yourself. The land full of bloody crimes is what came upon Jerusalem when this law was not applied among the people.

A lot of people do not know how to apply this verse; the precept for Leviticus 5:1 is Deuteronomy 17:4. Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed: make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

points: Touching any unclean thing, the carcase of an unclean beast or the uncleanness of man, leaves a soul unclean and guilty. This goes into eating, not mere contact; the classes have touched on this already, and it stands.

The touching itself pertained to the sacrifice: Israel was separated from their uncleanness that they die not when they defile the tabernacle, so a man that had touched the unclean thing could not come in to sacrifice. There is no more sacrifice, so the touching-defilement laws do not apply today; a brush of boar bristles is not sin.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

points: If a soul swear, pronouncing with his lips to do evil or to do good, and it be hid from him, when he knoweth of it he is guilty. Brothers say, I swear to God; watch your mouth.

A man was held accountable for whatever came out of his mouth; pronouncing with his lips and not performing it was sin. When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it, for better is it that thou shouldest not vow than that thou shouldest vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin. Christ set the same standard on the mouth: let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

points: When a man is guilty in one of these things, he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing, and bring his trespass offering, a female from the flock, a lamb or a kid of the goats, and the priest shall make an atonement for him concerning his sin.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

points: Israel took the nourishment of the Lord for granted, and he grew tired of the empty offerings: put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. He spake not unto our fathers concerning burnt offerings, but this thing commanded he: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people. He never wanted the sacrifices above obedience; today he does not want an apology or money in the plate, he wants you to obey his voice and repent.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

points: The offering scaled to what a man could bring: if he be not able to bring a lamb, two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering; and if he be not able to bring those, the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour, with no oil and no frankincense upon it, for it is a sin offering.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

points: If a soul commit a trespass and sin through ignorance in the holy things of the Lord, he brings a ram without blemish, with thy estimation by shekels of silver after the shekel of the sanctuary; he makes amends for the harm done in the holy thing and adds the fifth part thereto for the priest, and it shall be forgiven him.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

points: If a soul sin against any of the commandments, though he wist it not, yet is he guilty, and shall bear his iniquity. Though he is ignorant of it, the iniquity is still there; saying I did not know does not remove sin, and everyone still appears before the judgment seat of Christ when it is all said and done. The priest made an atonement concerning his ignorance wherein he erred and wist it not, for he hath certainly trespassed against the Lord.

The remedy is to know the law: let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord, and meditate continually in his commandments. The ordinances are found in the first five books; as these four chapters a day are conducted, meditate and study them continually.

Stay humble with it: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty; neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me; David behaved and quieted himself as a child that is weaned of his mother. Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven; so behave yourselves humbly, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness
